title: DreamShifter - A small game I made in 4 days for the Epic AI Megajam
author: LudumTremens
selftext:
Hello there!  
  
I've been working as a game dev for 16 years now. I lost my job recently (like a lot of people in the industry) and decided to try to make games on my own, which, by the way, is terrifying.  
I have a lot of experience in game design, writing and direction, so I know how to scope a game and define every piece of it, but I'm an absolute beginner at actual code implementation, art creation or even using the Unreal Engine.

I decided to join the Jam to learn as much as I could, and I worked really hard on it because even if there are ways to automatize lots of things with AI, I prefer to implement things step by step. After all, my craft lies in the tiny details and I don't want the AI to make any game design in my stead.

I'm pretty happy with the result (even though I have the classical Jam feeling of wanting to fix and change a lot of stuff), because it's a complete small game with innovative mechanics, collectibles, beginning, ending, coherence, and a reasonable level of polish.

I included a brief summary of how the game was made and its workflow on the itch page. I thought that it might be interesting for anyone hanging on this reddit.  
  
If you enjoy the game, please leave a comment on itch; I'll deeply appreciate it!  
If you want to ask anything or give me advice on how to better use AI, let's talk here!
